name: Connection Hygiene at Scale
description: Govern Fabric connections across a large tenant using connection-recency signals: find and safely retire stale and duplicate connections, and remove single-owner orphan risk. Keeps you under the 1,000-connection-per-gateway limit. All discovery steps are read-only; act only after human review.
prerequisites: Run as the identity that owns/administers the connections (cloud connections show only ones you own; a gateway admin sees all connections on that gateway)
Connection.Read.All (discovery) and Connection.ReadWrite.All / Owner (to delete or add owners)

steps.command: fabio connection list -o json --query "[].{name: displayName, bound: connectionRecency.lastBoundDateTime, used: connectionRecency.lastCredentialUsedDateTime}"
steps.description: Inspect the recency signals across all connections.
steps.notes: lastCredentialUsedDateTime can lag ~30 min — use for governance, not live monitoring.

steps.description: List stale candidates: never-bound, never-used, or credentials-unused for 90+ days.
steps.notes: Only connections created on/after --created-after (default 2026-05-01) are assessed, to avoid NULL-recency false positives on pre-GA connections.

steps.description: Extract the safest subset (never bound to any item) for retirement.
steps.notes: Review before deleting — some connections are seasonal (year-end/holiday runs).

steps.description: Find connections reaching the same target; the most-recently-used is kept (keepId), the rest are consolidation candidates.
steps.notes: Add --match-credential-type to treat different credential types as distinct targets.

steps.description: Find connections whose only Owner is an individual user — an orphan risk if they leave.
steps.notes: Issues one roleAssignments read per connection; skips connections it cannot read.

steps.description: Add a durable group owner to each single-owner connection.
steps.notes: A Microsoft Entra group survives member turnover; a second individual owner is better than one but not durable.

tips: Discovery commands are READ-ONLY — treat their output as a review list, not an automatic action list.
Gateways cap at 1,000 connections; regular hygiene keeps headroom.

A connection fails when its auth CREDENTIAL can no longer authenticate (e.g. OAuth tied to a deleted user), not merely because the owner account was deleted — SPN-based shared connections keep working.
Consolidate duplicates by repointing items to the keepId connection, then delete the redundant ones.
